items.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Med Flory plays two choruses, Lanny Morgan plays two choruses... I have to play after that, the vibes play.

ctx.x: And colleges are buying them left and right. I was just doing a clinic and a few of the college people said, “Are you kidding, we ordered fourteen.” Because they don’t write arrangements like that anymore. They’re just straight ahead swing music. And especially if you want to show the band off, if you play the arrangements like it’s really written, because I actually patterned the band after the Benny Goodman band because Benny played in and out. Because it didn’t blend with the section. It did, but it would…

items.title: Lanny Morgan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999
items.q: He worked locally and on the road with the bands of Charlie Barnet, Si Zentner and Terry Gibbs

ctx.x: Alto saxophonist Lanny Morgan was born on March 30, 1934 in DesMoines, Iowa. His family moved to Los Angeles in 1944 and he gained big band experience at Los Angeles City College. He worked locally and on the road with the bands of Charlie Barnet, Si Zentner and Terry Gibbs and in 1960 traveled to New York to join Maynard Ferguson’s band. Lanny was one of the principal soloists with this group, recording frequently and touring Europe in 1962. He has led an active career in west coast studios while performing with…
Lanny was interviewed in Los Angeles on February 14, 1999, by Monk Rowe, Director of the Hamilton College Jazz Archive.
